extracted.intended_audience: scientists, reviewers, and educated readers/contributors of Popular Science Monthly
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for critiquing scientific claims, experiments, and reviews in a learned magazine: covers experimental technique, use of evidence, quotations, mathematical correctness, terminology, statistics, and rhetoric/bias. Intended to inform peer-review-style commentary and editorial correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sterile technique and contamination control
rubrics_metrics.description: "no dust or particle from my clothes or body must be blown toward them... assistant ignites the spirit-lamp... thereby destroying all attached germs... snip off the sealed end... the same process is gone through, no flask being opened without the previous cleansing of the pliers by the flame."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe and follow detailed aseptic procedures (stand leeward, flame-sterilize instruments before opening, keep flask necks shaped to prevent ascent of contaminants). Example: twenty-seven flasks charged with mountain air remained free from life after months, illustrating effectiveness of technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of controls and comparative experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of flasks opened in free mountain air vs flasks opened in hay-loft: "twenty-seven putrescible infusions...have shown no sign of putrefaction... the others... the hay-loft invaded by organisms".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments with direct comparisons where only the variable of interest differs (same temperatures/handling). Use contemporaneous controls to support causal inferences (here, implicating dust particles rather than 'air' per se).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish fermentation from life; use precise terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: "With Liebig fermentation was by no means synonymous with life... whenever their author refers to this alleged power of decaying matter, he invariably couples with it the vague term 'fermentation,' thus softening the shock of the hypothesis..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague or equivocal terms that conflate distinct phenomena (e.g., fermentation vs generation of living organisms). State clearly what each term denotes and do not allow terminological looseness to obscure empirical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept authority blindly; verify with primary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: "So 'the best of authority' is sometimes at fault, and his conclusions are not always to be accepted blindly and without investigation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat eminent names and cited authorities critically; verify claims against primary data or methods (e.g., microscope observations) rather than relying on reputation alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate quotation and respect for context
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism of a misused Newton extract: "This extract... is in reality from two widely-separated parts of Newton's works, and is besides inaccurate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing sources, quote precisely and preserve context; do not splice or paraphrase in ways that change intended meaning. Misquotation can lead to erroneous conclusions and undermine arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical correctness and correct interpretation of quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuke of combining falling distances incorrectly: "Prof. Schneider's way of combining these numbers is unique... The .05386 is a part of .12084 ... the latter includes the former."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure numerical reasoning correctly interprets what quantities represent (subsets vs independent increments). Show work, diagram where helpful, and avoid aggregating incompatible measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate theoretical claims with observation and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is the practical proof of the correctness of the other view in the calculated and the observed positions of the moon for every hour of every day in every year... these positions being carefully noted by a score of observers every day."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support theoretical claims by comparing predictions to actual measurements and calculations. Use observational datasets to test competing theories rather than relying on deductive assertions alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and avoid private motives or conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspected bias in an article: "I am of opinion that the article alluded to has a private end to boost, 'a movement-cure institute,' perhaps, and I am fortified in this by the false points of the essay."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to potential conflicts of interest or hidden agendas; disclose affiliations or motives and avoid advocacy masquerading as impartial exposition. Readers should judge claims with awareness of possible bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise scientific language and maintain conceptual distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: "This is a very loose use of language... there is... a clear enough distinction between mechanical mixture and chemical combination, although Mr. [X] quite loses sight of it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make accurate, discipline-appropriate distinctions (e.g., mechanical mixture vs chemical hydrate). Loose wording can mislead; provide definitions or refer to authoritative sources when claims hinge on technical concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be current with literature and acknowledge timing of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial note: "It is but fair to say that the article in question was written and in the hands of the editor six months before Prof. Wright's researches were published.— Ed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate claims relative to the most recent relevant work; if new findings have appeared, acknowledge them and, where appropriate, revise interpretations. Note publication/timing constraints candidly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate sample size and representativeness; cautious inference
rubrics_metrics.description: "Although the statistics presented in the essay are, unfortunately, much smaller than is desirable... they are the most extensive published up to this time on the subject... Since the addition of his results... does not in any way conflict with the conclusions... it may be doubted whether more extensive general statistics would throw any further light on the subject."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample sizes and limits; avoid overgeneralizing from small or unrepresentative samples. Specify what further data would be needed to strengthen conclusions and indicate when results should remain provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define technical terms and justify any specialized usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate over terms: "the reviewer curiously misinterprets... 'rhythmic'... 'reproduction' used as equivalent for the process by which material is accumulated in the parent organism... This restriction is justified by examples..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly define any terms used in non-standard or specialized senses and justify those choices (give examples or cite authorities). Anticipate potential misreadings and clarify intended meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control confounding variables; seek 'pure' experiments where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every one knows that no pure experiment is possible unless all conditions are eliminated except the one whose influence is to be estimated. The difficulties in the way exactly resemble... those besetting... investigations concerning the influence of damp soils..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design studies to minimize confounders; acknowledge when true isolation is impossible and discuss implications for causal claims. Where control is limited, use careful comparative methods and transparency about limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align practical recommendations with evidence and humane feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "The closing sentence... observes that, wherever such women are engaged in industrial or other pursuits under an employer, humanity would dictate that as much rest be afforded as practicable during the period of suffering."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure policy or practical recommendations follow logically from the data and consider real-world constraints and humane considerations. Avoid prescribing remedies not supported by evidence or impractical in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check translations and linguistic accuracy in source materials
rubrics_metrics.description: "This may, however, be a translator's stumble." (on the lungs being described as mucous surface)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify translated passages against originals when possible; be cautious about relying on translations for technical claims and correct obvious translator errors or ambiguities before using them as evidence.
